sections.history: Thirukkannangudi lies about two kilometres from Sikkal, off the Tiruvarur–Nagapattinam highway in the Kaveri delta. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Chola Nadu. Thirumangai Alvar praised the Lord here in ten hymns of the Periya Thirumozhi. The temple is generally held to have been built by the Medieval Cholas in the late ninth century, though one account places it in the eighth. It is counted among the Pancha Krishnaranya Kshetrams, the five sacred groves of Krishna.
sections.architecture: The temple faces east and is entered through a five-tiered rajagopuram. The sanctum is crowned by the Utpala Vimanam, and the sacred tank is the Shravana Theertham, also called the Nithya Pushkarini in one temple listing. Behind the temple stands the sthala vriksham, a Magizha tree, said never to die. The presiding Lord is Loganatha Perumal with the Goddess Loganayagi, and the festival image is Damodara Narayana Perumal with Aravindavalli.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Vasishta, who worshipped a butter image of Krishna that did not melt. Krishna came to him as a child and swallowed it, and Vasishta followed him to this place, where, by the power of devotion, the child was bound to the Magizha tree. The festival image shows Krishna so bound by a rope, as Damodara. Tradition adds that Thirumangai Alvar, tired and thirsty, rested under the Magizha tree and was given food and water by the Lord, who appeared with conch and discus and then vanished.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Vaishnava calendar, with Vaikunta Ekadashi among its observances; confirm specific festival dates locally. The festival image of Damodara, bound to the Magizha tree with a rope, is the heart of the shrine's devotion, and it is this form that devotees remember in the temple's days of worship.
sections.experience: A quiet, devotional Divya Desam close to Sikkal, rewarding for pilgrims tracing Thirumangai Alvar's hymns through the delta. Look for the Magizha tree behind the temple and for the festival image of Krishna bound as Damodara. Early visits are calm; confirm timings locally before you go.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is about two kilometres from Sikkal, off the Tiruvarur–Nagapattinam highway, in the Nagapattinam district of Tamil Nadu. Nagapattinam and Tiruvarur are the nearest larger towns with railheads, and Tiruchirappalli is the nearest major airport. Reach it by road, and confirm local directions on arrival.
